Core concepts

The ideas every other page builds on — ADOM, appliance, the device cache and source of truth, jobs, scheduled actions, change requests, profiles and permissions, processes and templates.

👤 ForViewerOperatorAdministrator
📍 WhereApplies across the whole console

How the pieces fit#

  1. 1Register an applianceIt belongs to one product ADOM
  2. 2Discover itRediscovery / Deep capture fill SATOM's own copy of its configuration
  3. 3Work from the copyPages are fast and work even when the box is not
  4. 4Change itPreview → confirm → applied, snapshotted and audited
  5. 5Run long work as jobsTrack them in the job dock and the Jobs page
  6. 6Automate and controlScheduled actions repeat work; change requests gate risky work

ADOM#

A workspace scoped to one product family: Global, FortiWeb, FortiADC, FortiAuthenticator or FortiAnalyzer. Each ADOM has its own menu and only sees its own appliances and records; Global sees everything. The ADOM is remembered per browser tab. → ADOMs and products

Appliance#

A Fortinet device registered in SATOM: name, product (Kind), management address and port, credentials (stored encrypted), and classification (Zone, Line, Department, Tags). An appliance can be a single box or an HA cluster (node 0 plus member nodes). An appliance in maintenance mode is hidden from users without the permission to see maintenance devices. → Appliances

Device cache, snapshots and the source of truth#

SATOM keeps its own copy of each appliance's configuration so pages can be rendered without contacting the box:

  • Rediscovery — one read-only sweep that re-reads every configuration object of the appliance. The first run is called Discovery.
  • Deep capture — follows server policies and web protection profiles into their dependencies (members, rule lists, disabled signatures, exceptions) for the analysis pages. Optional and slower.
  • Source of truth (SoT) — a versioned history of each appliance's configuration. Each version is a snapshot identified by the hash of its content, so an unchanged configuration creates no new version.

Because pages read the copy, what you see can be behind the appliance; use the page's refresh-from-device control when you need the live state. → Rediscovery, Data and storage

ℹ️Note

A backup is different from a snapshot: it is the appliance's own configuration file, kept in the per-appliance backup vault so it can be downloaded or restored. → Backups

Preview before apply#

Changes to an appliance are prepared, shown as a preview of exactly what will be sent, and only written when you confirm. The write is snapshotted and recorded with before/after detail in the Audit Log.

Job#

Anything long — a backup, a discovery, a bulk change, a firmware transfer — runs as a background job. A dock in the corner of the screen tracks it while you keep navigating, and the Jobs page lists running and finished jobs with Pause, Resume and Stop. You control your own jobs; administrators control everyone's. Stopping is cooperative: the job stops at its next safe point, never in the middle of a device write. → Jobs

Scheduled action (Automations)#

A unit of work that runs on a schedule without anyone clicking. The scheduler fires them on the primary node. There are two lists:

Page What it holds Who
Automations (Automation menu) Fleet work somebody planned for a chosen time — a cutover, draining a backend, a certificate swap or renewal, an upgrade, a reboot, an HA failover. Upgrade, reboot, HA failover, the Cert Manager lifecycle sweep and Custom REST calls run only bound to an approved change request, inside its window. Users with write access
System Automations (Administrator → System) SATOM maintaining itself — backups, source-of-truth syncs, probe sweeps, signature and CVE refreshes. SATOM creates the default set when the node gets its first appliance. Administrators

→ Scheduled actions

Change request#

The control record for a risky change done inside a maintenance window — above all a firmware upgrade: which appliances and policies are affected, when, an approval step, and the one-shot scheduled action that executes it inside the window. A live FortiWeb firmware upgrade is refused unless an approved change request names the appliance and its maintenance window is open (a dry run is allowed without one). The Upgrade Flow page chains pre-upgrade checks, one change request, the customer-impact export and execution for many appliances at once. → Change requests, Upgrade flow

Profile and permission#

A permission is one granular right, such as backups.create or protection.apply. A profile is a named set of permissions assigned to a user. Three profiles ship with SATOM:

Profile In short
readonly Read access to every section; cannot change anything.
operator Read everything plus manage appliances, protection, network, backups and operations. No user or registry administration.
admin Full access, including users and profiles.

Administrators can create other profiles from the permission catalog. Menu entries you cannot use are hidden, and every page checks again on the server. → Users and profiles, Permissions

Runbooks#

A procedure — a recovery plan, a post-upgrade validation, an onboarding check — is a Plugin Studio app: checks SATOM runs itself, and questions that wait for a person on the run page. Simulate walks it as a rehearsal. (The Process section that did this until 2026-10-25 was removed.) → Plugin Studio apps

Template#

Versioned desired state kept in the Template Library. A template is saved as a pending draft, approved by an administrator to become fleet-deployable, and can be applied to an appliance as a separate, audited action. → Template library

Audit trail#

Sign-ins, configuration changes, sharing a bookmark, approving a template and other actions are written to the Audit Log with who, when and what. → Audit log

See also the Glossary for every other term used in the console.
